title: Japan tour: factory concerts and gracious audiences
summary: He found Japan receptive; on a twelve-week contract they toured cities and played auditorium concerts for factory shifts as the only American band there.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Okay, in Japan now, what do you remember about that, the most significant thing of that trip?

Japan, to my humble opinion, is a first-class country. Very receptive, ahh very -- here they say polite, but I think they are that way because we wasn't there saving no life, we was playing music and they treat us like kings. Full of respect, very gracious to me about everything and we had a tremendous time.
Did they appreciate your tipico stuff or .....
Was it intended for you to stay there three months or is that .....
No, the contract, the contract lasts for three months.....
... and did you play the same place all the time?
No, first we did a tour for the principal cities up there ...
... and we played practically every industry, because in those areas, I don't know if they still do it, they used to work twenty-four hours, so every eight hours they had a concert.
You mean you went to a factory and played for ....
They had auditorium, beautiful!! We had good sound and well-prepared the pianos, everything was ...
Were you the only North American band there in Japan at that time?
